attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his newsletter, describing his own earlier warnings and asserting they are now happening.

semantics.note: An unhedged present-tense claim that the warned-about harms are 'all happening'. The normalisation keeps all three named harms and correctly leaves out 'and so on'.

contract.note: Marcus named no measures, so this is a plain reading. Using 2025 as the period, requiring AI involvement without requiring sole causation, and separating scam attempts, victims and losses are ordinary, fair readings. The result still depends on these interpretations because no scope or thresholds were given.

evidence.note: Marcus's 2023 post shows he warned about AI-driven enshittification and misinformation. It shows the warnings existed, not that the harms occurred. No earlier warning about cyberscams is shown.

A study sampled in early 2025 found about 5% AI slop among biomedical education videos and called it not especially prevalent. It covers one narrow area, so it neither shows nor rules out web-wide deterioration.
NewsGuard measured AI-enabled Russian false narratives about France, Dec 2024–Mar 2025, reaching about 55.8M views. This supports large-audience spread of AI-enabled misinformation in the period.
Data from one vendor, Sumsub: its identity-fraud rate fell from 2024 to 2025 while sophisticated attacks grew. Its coverage is too narrow to settle a broader rise in cyberscams.

FBI IC3: total complaints rose from 2024 to 2025, but that category is broader than scams. The AI-related complaint count has no earlier figure to compare against, so it does not show AI-enabled scams increasing.

reviews.rationale: The misinformation part holds: NewsGuard measured AI-enabled false narratives reaching tens of millions of views in the period. Web enshittification is shown only in one narrow sample, whose authors found slop not especially prevalent. No comparable evidence shows AI-involved scams increasing, and no earlier warning about cyberscams was found. Nothing contradicts any part, but the support condition requires all three harms, so the claim as a whole is not settled.
